title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Freelancer. Tip #1
body: Ask what he does and watch the sentence take four attempts. There is no clean Azerbaijani word for it, so he says "onlayn işləyirəm" and a relative immediately assumes it isn't real. He has stopped fighting this. Ask what platform. Upwork means he's serious, Fiverr means he started there, direct clients means he's won. It's a sealed deal if his grandmother believes he is unemployed and he has made peace with it.
caption:
Tip #1 😭 frilanserlər, your family still thinks you're jobless.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Freelancer. Tip #2
body: Ask how he gets paid, because that is the entire drama of freelancing in this country. Payoneer, Wise, a card that stopped working in March, or crypto he'd rather not discuss. Every freelancer here has had one payment stuck somewhere for three weeks. It's a sealed deal if he can explain the fee structure of three payment platforms without pausing.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Freelancer. Tip #3
body: Watch the hours. The clients are American, so the calls are at 10pm, and he has been living on a European schedule inside an Azerbaijani household for two years. His family eats at eight. He works at eleven. Nobody has adjusted. It's a sealed deal if his mother has knocked during a client call and appeared on camera.
caption:
Tip #3 😭 frilanserlər, your family still thinks you're jobless.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Freelancer. Tip #4
body: Ask about the first big client, because there is always one, and losing them is the story that made him professional. Now there are three, deliberately, because he learned. He has a contract template. He asks for a deposit. He got both of those from an expensive mistake. It's a sealed deal if he can name the exact month the money stopped and what he did that week.
caption:
Tip #4 😭 frilanserlər, your family still thinks you're jobless.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Freelancer. Tip #5
body: Look at where he works. A café until the wifi betrayed him, then a corner of the flat, then eventually an actual desk. The desk was a big purchase and a bigger statement. Coffee Moffie and the laptop crowd are a whole ecosystem and they all recognise each other. It's a sealed deal if he has a specific seat in a specific café near a specific socket and gets quietly annoyed when it's taken.

Tip #5 😭 frilanserlər, your family still thinks you're jobless.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Freelancer. Tip #6
body: Ask what he tells people at weddings. He has a short version for relatives, a real version for friends, and a completely different one for anyone who might be a client. All three are true. The relative version is the shortest and involves the word "kompüter." It's a sealed deal if an uncle has offered to find him a real job in the last twelve months.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku Freelancer. Tip #7
body: Ask about tax and watch the temperature change. Everybody is somewhere on a spectrum between fully registered and hoping. Some went to ASAN and did it properly. Some have a friend who explained it wrong in 2022. Nobody enjoys this conversation. It's a sealed deal if he changes the subject to exchange rates within fifteen seconds.
